description: This is a Java source class defining a custom ViewGroup called FoldingLayout, which implements a foldable UI component with adjustable number of folds, orientation, anchor point, and fold factor. It manages drawing of its single child view with real-time folding transformations and shading effects.

classes.name: FoldingLayout
classes.description: A customizable foldable layout that manages rendering its single child with perspective fold transformations.

classes.name: Orientation
classes.description: Enumeration for folding orientation: VERTICAL or HORIZONTAL.

classes.name: NumberOfFoldingLayoutChildrenException
classes.description: Runtime exception thrown when more than one child is added to the FoldingLayout.

methods.name: addViewInLayout
methods.description: Overrides method to prevent adding more than one child.

methods.name: addView
methods.description: Overrides method to prevent adding more than one child.

methods.name: onLayout
methods.description: Positions the single child view and updates folding matrices.

methods.name: throwCustomException
methods.description: Throws exception if there is more than one child view.

methods.name: setFoldListener
methods.description: Registers a listener for fold events.

methods.name: setFoldFactor
methods.description: Sets the fold factor (0 to 1) and updates transformation matrices.

methods.name: setAnchorFactor
methods.description: Sets the anchor point factor for folding.

methods.name: setNumberOfFolds
methods.description: Sets how many folds the layout will have.

methods.name: updateFold
methods.description: Repairs the fold setup with updated parameters.

methods.name: prepareFold
methods.description: Initializes matrices and calculations necessary for folding with specific parameters.

methods.name: calculateMatrices
methods.description: Computes transformation matrices for each fold segment based on current fold factor.

methods.name: dispatchDraw
methods.description: Custom drawing method that renders the folded content with perspective transformations and shadows.
